US midterm shock reshapes the commodity outlook. Gold and silver rally on a weaker dollar and lower yields, oil slides on hopes of an Iran deal, while copper reassesses tariff risks. Political gridlock ahead, but Trump retains considerable power over trade and foreign policy. https://t.co/98Pt3ZiBy6 via @saxobank

US midterms response across key commodities: The Democrats' historic election victory has triggered an initial reassessment of US fiscal, trade and foreign policy, with precious metals emerging as the clear winners.

Precious metals: Gold and silver have rallied, supported by a softer dollar and lower Treasury yields amid expectations that a Democrat-controlled Congress could constrain Trump's fiscal agenda and limit further, increasingly unaffordable fiscal expansion. Short covering has added momentum after gold reclaimed key resistance at USD 3,970, potentially setting up a challenge of the downtrend in place since August, currently around USD 4,035.

Copper: Prices trade lower but off their lows as traders reassess AI-related demand prospects and whether Trump's defeat, combined with voters' focus on affordability, has reduced the likelihood of US import tariffs on refined copper. Such a shift could ease short-term supply distortions and potentially release US-held inventories back onto the global market, while longer-term supply constraints remain supportive.

Energy: Oil prices have staged a modest rebound following a two-day slump as traders weigh conflicting signals over the prospects for US-Iran peace talks. Adding to the uncertainty is how Trump may respond on the foreign policy front, where his executive powers remain considerable despite a resounding electoral rebuke driven by voter frustration over the cost of living and the war in Iran. With his domestic agenda now facing greater congressional resistance, the risk of a more assertive stance abroad cannot be ignored, keeping geopolitical uncertainty firmly in focus.

GRIT (9243150) is a supertanker that recently transported Iraqi crude oil to the Gulf of Oman. Iran's PGSA recently doubled its list of tankers to target, and roughly 30% of the cargo aboard those tankers is Iraqi. This serves as a reminder that Iraq is not immune to the IRGC.
